advances: A compactness result for actual unit-normal hinge covers and their existing finite stress data.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Choose a ball $RB_d$ containing all fibers. The uniform hinge bound gives a uniform lower bound on each cap threshold at each sampled base because the contribution of a fiber of volume $V$ at threshold $t$ is at least $V(-R-t)_+$. Along a subsequence the normals converge on their unit sphere and each affine threshold sequence has a finite or $+\infty$ limit. Work with one cap, write its affine threshold coefficients as $w_k$ and let $I$ be the bases with finite limits. The evaluation image on $I$ is a closed subspace, so some coefficient vector $w_0$ realizes the finite limits. Let $E_I$ denote evaluation on $I$ and $J$ a linear right inverse on its image. The residual $w_k-w_0-J(E_I(w_k-w_0))$ vanishes on $I$ and tends to $+\infty$ at every other base. If any other bases exist, fix one such residual $h$ strictly positive at all of them. Then the bounded replacement coefficients
$$
w'_k=w_0+J(E_I(w_k-w_0))+Th
$$
with $T$ fixed sufficiently large agree on $I$ and give thresholds at least $R+1$ elsewhere for all large $k$. If all bases are in $I$, use the same formula with the last term zero. Empty $I$ has zero evaluation image. This is the affine kernel construction used in 0a73ba4a9c7b24d1, retaining the varying bounded coordinates. Repeat for each cap.

For large $k$, the old and new thresholds outside their respective sets $I$ are at least $R+1$. Thus all these margins are at most $-1$ on their fibers. The other traces have identical margins at every point, and this equality persists under any common coefficient increment. Uniformly small increments, bounded using the compact measured set and finitely many coefficient blocks, make the omitted margins at most $-3/4$. At every point there is a nonomitted margin at least zero before perturbation by the old coverage, so some nonomitted margin is at least $-1/4$ afterwards. Therefore the cap-mass and hinge functions are unchanged under these common increments, and so are the pointwise maxima and the fiberwise minimum-of-maximum coverage functions. The same local functions have identical generalized gradients at the corresponding parameters. The replacements converge to bounded affine parameters, their pointwise maxima converge uniformly on the measured set, and the limit covers. Cap masses and cap first moments converge by dominated convergence using the fiber-volume-null cutting planes.

For the stress limit, the sum of the offset balances gives $\sum_z\eta_z=\sum_i c_i+\sum_i r_iS_i$. The section masses have a fixed upper bound by the enclosing ball and finite number of fibers, with counting sections in dimension one. Thus the contact multipliers are bounded as well. Take convergent subsequences of all scalar multipliers. The saddle probabilities on $K_z\times\Delta_N$ for positive limiting multipliers have weakly convergent subsequences on these compact spaces. Their limits are supported on actual saddle pairs by uniform convergence of the finite margin functions and the defining two saddle inequalities. Terms at bases of zero limiting multiplier vanish. At every active contact, the limiting fiber coverage is zero and positive weights are supported on zero-margin caps. In particular no omitted trace has positive saddle weight. The finite collection of moments $p_{zi},q_{zi}$ of each limiting law can be reproduced by a finite convex combination of saddle features by finite-dimensional Carathéodory, since those features form a compact set.

On each fiber, move the varying section plane to its limiting plane by isometries tending to the identity. The transported section measures have bounded support and are dominated by plane $\mathcal H^{d-1}$. Weak subsequential limits retain domination and are supported in the actual limiting section by closedness. If the limiting cut is proper, the nearby cuts are proper, and section indicators in the limiting plane converge almost everywhere after the isometries. Indeed, a relative interior point of a proper section is in the interior of the body, while a point outside the closed section stays outside; the relative boundary is null. Thus the limiting density is one on proper cuts. In dimension one the same reasoning uses counting measure at the single section point, with the continuous normal signs constant along the subsequence. On supporting cuts the dominated limit has density between zero and one. These measures give simultaneous limits of all zeroth and first moments. Taking limits of the three stress equations gives the objective-one moment form. The coverage and budget complementarity equations follow by continuity, with the budget equations using the convergent budgets.

statement: Let $S$ be a finite union of fixed positive polytopal fibers at integer bases, with summed volume. Consider a sequence of full covers of $S$ by the same finite number of closed affine caps with Euclidean unit continuous normals, with bounded total hinge. After taking a subsequence, one can replace each cap by one with bounded affine coefficients, preserving all its traces on $S$ and preserving the cap-mass, hinge, and fiber coverage functions under all sufficiently small common parameter increments. The resulting parameters have a limit defining a finite full cover. If the original covers have objective-one normal stress data in the sense of d83edebb7d5b8852 with bounded sums of nonnegative budget multipliers, a subsequence of their stresses yields an objective-one stress of the same moment and saddle form for that limit cover. Complementarity and feasibility pass when the budgets converge.
title: Bounded trace representatives and compactness of actual hinge stresses
